name: MUSES01 / NJM5720
type: J-FET-input dual audio op-amp, OFC lead frame, DIP8
tagline: New JRC's JFET flagship and the first op-amp with an OFC lead frame; Japan's answer to the OPA627.

lineage.note: NJM5720 mass production announced May 2009 (PHILE WEB); English datasheet and hobby sales followed December 2009.
Took over New JRC's semiconductor business; the 2025-03-21 datasheet marks MUSES01 NRND.

part_numbers.note: DIP8 dual only; 150 dB channel separation. DigiKey 2202385, LCSC/JLCPCB C4548949.
Akizuki's name for the same part (catalogue g103416); absent from vendor datasheet.
Original NJM number of the same product; Akizuki lists 'MUSES01D (NJM5720)'.

reputation.summary: One of Japan's most admired audio op-amps, often treated as a domestic OPA627 and compared head-to-head in e-earphone, mixi and blog shoot-outs. Listeners report a wide soundstage and very smooth, refined, extended treble; one notes slightly weak impact. Genre folklore is inconsistent. No independent bench measurements exist, so the praise rests on listening.
typical_uses: Audio preamps, active filters and line amps (datasheet)
Op-amp rolling in DACs, car audio, headphone amps (±9 V+)
High-end Japanese DIY headphone amps, I/V and buffers
caveats: NRND per vendor datasheet, DigiKey and Mouser; MUSES02 too. MUSES03/05 reportedly discontinued.
Needs ±9 to ±16 V, ruling out 5 V, ±5 V and battery rails (MUSES02 runs from ±3.5 V).
Bias 200 pA typ / 800 pA max is high for JFET and rises with heat; offset 5 mV max.
Common-mode range only ±8 V min on ±15 V rails, limiting large-swing unity-gain buffers.
Costly, widely faked and DIP8 only; soft OFC leads reportedly bend easily. Praise is listening-only.

counterfeit_notes: Fakes are common (fakecomponents on X, Japanese blogs). Genuine: flat grey-white laser marking, sharp goddess logo. Fakes: raised white ink, blurred logo; reportedly stiff leads, misplaced pin-1 dot. Only DIP8 duals exist. Marking varies by lot; buy authorised.

revision_history.changes: Mass production of NJM5720 began: MUSES J-FET dual, OFC lead frame, DIP8 only. A product event, not a datasheet.
Reported Japanese launch datasheet (Akizuki file name); unconfirmed. JRC datasheets carry no change log.
English launch version (Qobuz mirror). No change log.
Mouser 259020 and yibeiic copies; same headline specs (9.5 nV/√Hz, 12 V/µs, 3.3 MHz, 200 pA). Changes unknown.
alldatasheet.jp 2278441 Nisshinbo copy (2022 or later; 656 KB, 12 pages); may equal 20250321.
NRND reissue: NRND notice on every page, Nisshinbo MUSES trademark, bare YYYYMMDD footer. Specs unchanged. MUSES02 (20250319) reissued likewise.

revision_chains.note: Known only from an Akizuki file name; unconfirmed.
Unidentified: Mouser 1917225, alldatasheet.jp 2278441, alldatasheet 808059, dtsheet 1304583, SlideShare 16286764. No PCN found.

open_questions: Which revisions do the legacy njr.com PDF, Mouser 1917225, alldatasheet 347303/2278441 and file 679182 copies hold?
Does the Japanese Ver.2009-12-11 exist on Akizuki? The catalogue page is confirmed, the PDF link is not.
Did the 2009 and 2015 revisions also specify ±9 V to ±16 V operation?
When was NRND declared, and is there a last-time-buy date? Check Nisshinbo's discontinued-products page.
When did MUSES01 supersede NJM5720 as the main name? Did any Nisshinbo-era lot change its marking style?

claims_confirmed: MUSES01 is NRND at DigiKey (not normally stocked) and Mouser: https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/nisshinbo-micro-devices-inc/MUSES01/2202385, https://www.mouser.com/ProductDetail/Nisshinbo/MUSES01?qs=yQ3iditm8N7pF0xkkmEW4g%3D%3D
Nisshinbo publishes an NRND list page: https://www.nisshinbo-microdevices.co.jp/en/design-support/discon/
NJM5720 mass production: MUSES J-FET dual, world's first high-purity OFC lead frame, DIP8 only: https://www.phileweb.com/news/audio/200905/20/8964.html
Nisshinbo English product page 'MUSES01 Series' exists: https://www.nisshinbo-microdevices.co.jp/en/products/operational-amplifier/spec/?product=muses01
alldatasheet 347303 holds a 12-page, 528 KB NJRC copy: https://www.alldatasheet.com/datasheet-pdf/pdf/347303/NJRC/MUSES01.html

Distributors list 9.5 nV/√Hz, 12 V/µs, 3.3 MHz, 200 pA, ±9 to ±16 V: https://www.microchipusa.com/product/nisshinbo-micro-devices-inc/instrumentation-op-amps-buffer-amps/MUSES01, https://www.endrich.com/en/product-categories/active-components/analog-and-discrete/operational-amplifier/muses01
Genuine marking is flat grey-white laser engraving; fakes use thick white ink and a blurred goddess logo: https://maimai-audio.blog.jp/archives/40081909.html
Fake MUSES01 listings documented on Japanese marketplaces: https://x.com/fakecomponents/status/895845393963012096

e-earphone shoot-out and mixi MUSES01/MUSES02/OPA627 comparison describe a wide soundstage and very smooth sound: https://e-earphone.blog/?p=46602, https://mixi.jp/view_diary.pl?id=1952300790&owner_id=340485
refuted_claims: 'MUSES01D may not be a real orderable name' is refuted: Akizuki sells 'MUSES01D (NJM5720)' (https://akizukidenshi.com/catalog/g/g103416/).
'MUSES01 for J-POP/vocals, MUSES02 for jazz/classical' is contradicted by other Japanese comparisons; genre folklore is inconsistent.
NJM5720 was not a pre-MUSES name renamed in December 2009: PHILE WEB announced it as a MUSES part in May 2009.
